text: {"brief_summary":"Example Distribution FZE is a building-materials distributor with about 80 staff and one central warehouse in Jebel Ali. Stock levels are kept in spreadsheets updated at the end of each day, so sales staff often promise goods that are not on the shelf. The customer wants four things: warehouse staff recording goods received and dispatched as they happen, sales staff seeing current stock per product before confirming an order, reorder alerts when stock is low, and a monthly stock valuation report for finance. The company uses an accounting package for invoicing, and how it would connect is not yet known. Warehouse staff use handheld devices, and Wi-Fi is patchy in some aisles. The budget is fixed and the first version should be live in four months.","technology_stack":{"title":"Technology stack for stock control","question":"Which platform should the stock control solution be built on or configured from?","context":"Fact: the brief names no technology. It asks for real-time receipt and dispatch recording on handheld devices in a warehouse with patchy Wi-Fi, live stock visibility for sales, reorder alerts, a monthly valuation report and a possible link to an existing accounting package. The budget is fixed and the first version is due in four months. Assumption: the company has no in-house development team and limited IT staff, given its size (about 80 staff) and its current use of spreadsheets.","options":[{"key":"saas_inventory","title":"Configured SaaS inventory product","description":"Subscribe to and configure an off-the-shelf cloud inventory product, for example Zoho Inventory, Odoo Inventory or Cin7. licensing could strain a fixed budget","Valuation logic and stock movement rules must be built rather than configured","Accounting integration would need a custom or premium connector","Needs someone to maintain the app after go-live"]},{"key":"custom_cloud_app","title":"Custom offline-capable web app on Azure or AWS","description":"Build a bespoke progressive web app with local offline storage and sync for the handhelds, a web view for sales, and a cloud database and API.","pros":["Full control over offline behaviour and the handheld experience","Can be shaped exactly to the company's products and processes","No per-user licence fees"],"cons":["Highest build effort and risk against a four-month deadline and a fixed budget","Valuation, alerts and accounting integration all built from scratch","The company would depend on the supplier for maintenance and hosting"]}],"recommended_option":"saas_inventory","recommendation_rationale":"The requested features are standard inventory functions (brief), and the budget is fixed with a four-month deadline (brief). A configured product is the lowest-risk way to meet both. Ready-made accounting connectors also give the best chance of handling the unknown accounting package. This recommendation depends on two checks before selection: that the chosen product works on the existing handhelds, and that it handles patchy Wi-Fi acceptably. If no shortlisted product passes both checks, Power Platform is the fallback.","assumptions":["The company has no in-house developers and limited IT capacity","The accounting package is a mainstream product with available connectors","Building-materials products can be modelled within a standard inventory product, including units of measure","The existing handhelds can run a vendor mobile app or a browser"],"risks":["The SaaS mobile app may not work offline, leaving receipts unrecorded in poor-Wi-Fi aisles","The existing handhelds may be incompatible, adding unbudgeted hardware cost","The accounting package may have no connector, forcing manual exports or custom work","Subscription costs over time may exceed what a fixed budget allows"],"source_quotes":["Warehouse staff use handheld devices; the warehouse has patchy Wi-Fi in some aisles.","The company uses an accounting package for invoicing; how it would connect is not known yet.","The budget is fixed and the first version should be live in four months."]},"delivery_approach":{"title":"Delivery approach","question":"How should the first version be delivered and rolled out within four months?","context":"Fact: there is one central warehouse, and the core problem is that sales staff promise goods that are not on the shelf. Assumption: moving off spreadsheets will need a physical stock count to set opening balances.","options":[{"key":"phased_mvp","title":"Phased MVP, then increments","description":"First release: product catalogue, opening stock, real-time receipts and dispatches on handhelds, and live stock visibility for sales. Later increments add reorder alerts, the monthly valuation report and the accounting integration.","pros":["Tackles the main problem (promising unavailable stock) first","Keeps the four-month date realistic even if the accounting connection turns out to be complex","Lets the fixed budget be spent on what matters most first"],"cons":["Finance waits for the valuation report unless it is pulled into the first release","Integration remains open after go-live, so some manual reconciliation continues","Needs clear agreement on what counts as the first version"]},{"key":"pilot_then_rollout","title":"Pilot on a product range or area, then full rollout","description":"Run the full solution for one product category or warehouse zone for a few weeks, alongside the spreadsheets, before switching the whole warehouse over.","pros":["Tests handhelds and Wi-Fi coverage in real conditions before full commitment","Lower risk of disrupting dispatches"],"cons":["With one warehouse, running two methods side by side is confusing for sales","Stock visibility is only partial during the pilot","Uses time from a tight four-month window"]},{"key":"single_release","title":"Single full release","description":"Deliver all four features and the accounting integration together at the four-month mark.","pros":["One cutover and one round of training","Finance gets the valuation report from day one"],"cons":["Depends on the unknown accounting integration, which puts the date at risk","No early feedback from warehouse staff on handheld use","Any overrun hits a fixed budget with no fallback scope"]}],"recommended_option":"phased_mvp","recommendation_rationale":"The brief's core pain point is sales promising stock that is not there. Real-time receipts and dispatches plus live stock visibility fix that directly. The accounting connection is explicitly unknown, so keeping it out of the first release protects the four-month date and the fixed budget. Reorder alerts and the valuation report are often standard in a SaaS product and could be included early at little cost. A short handheld and Wi-Fi test in the worst aisles should come before go-live, rather than a full pilot.","assumptions":["The customer agrees that the first version need not include the accounting integration","A full stock count can be done shortly before go-live to load opening balances","Finance can tolerate an interim valuation approach if the report comes in a later increment"],"risks":["The customer may consider the valuation report or integration mandatory for the first version","Inaccurate opening stock would undermine trust in the new system from day one","Staff may keep using spreadsheets in parallel unless the cutover is firm","Later increments may have little budget left under a fixed budget"],"source_quotes":["so sales staff often promise goods that are not on the shelf.","The budget is fixed and the first version should be live in four months.","The company uses an accounting package for invoicing; Must staff be able to record receipts and dispatches offline and sync later, or is improving Wi-Fi coverage an option?","why_it_matters":"Offline capability strongly narrows the platform choice. Without it, real-time recording fails exactly where the brief says connectivity is weak.","suggested_answers":[{"key":"offline_sync","title":"Full offline with later sync","description":"Devices store transactions locally and sync when back in coverage."},{"key":"improve_wifi","title":"Improve Wi-Fi coverage","description":"The customer adds access points so an always-online app works everywhere."},{"key":"record_at_dock","title":"Record at covered points only","description":"Staff scan at receiving and dispatch areas that have good coverage."}],"recommended_answer":"offline_sync","recommendation_rationale":"The brief states patchy Wi-Fi as a known condition. Offline recording with sync is the common way to keep stock accurate without depending on network upgrades outside this project's scope.","source_quotes":["Warehouse staff use handheld devices; the warehouse has patchy Wi-Fi in some aisles.","Warehouse staff record goods received and goods dispatched as they happen."]},{"category":"business_rules","title":"Stock valuation method","question":"Which valuation method does finance use for the monthly stock valuation report, and what should the report show?","why_it_matters":"The valuation method determines how costs are captured at goods receipt and whether a SaaS product's standard report is acceptable. It may also need to match the accounting package.","suggested_answers":[{"key":"weighted_average","title":"Weighted average cost","description":"Value stock at the running average purchase cost."},{"key":"fifo","title":"FIFO","description":"Value stock as if the oldest units are sold first."},{"key":"standard_cost","title":"Standard or last purchase cost","description":"Use a set cost per product, reviewed periodically."}],"recommended_answer":null,"recommendation_rationale":"","source_quotes":["A monthly stock valuation report for finance."]},{"category":"business_rules","title":"Reorder alert rules","question":"Who sets the reorder levels for each product, who should receive low-stock alerts, and how should they be delivered (email, in-app, daily summary)?","why_it_matters":"This defines the alert logic, the roles involved and the data that must be loaded for each product before go-live.","suggested_answers":[{"key":"fixed_min_levels","title":"Fixed minimum per product","description":"Purchasing sets a minimum quantity per product; alerts go to the purchasing team."},{"key":"usage_based","title":"Usage-based levels","description":"Reorder levels are calculated from recent sales and supplier lead time."},{"key":"daily_digest","title":"Daily low-stock digest","description":"A single daily list of products below minimum instead of individual alerts."}],"recommended_answer":"fixed_min_levels","recommendation_rationale":"Fixed minimums are simple to set up from current knowledge and are supported by most products.
